title: MIT Made a Black So Dark a $2 Million Diamond Looks Flat

scenes.text: Scientists made a black so dark, a diamond looks flat.
It's a coating of tiny carbon nanotubes grown on aluminum foil.
It soaks up 99.995 percent of the light that hits it.
MIT coated a yellow diamond worth two million dollars with it.
The sparkling gem turned into a flat black void.
They found it by accident, while trying to improve aluminum.

description:
Scientists made a black so dark, a diamond looks flat.
MIT engineers grew carbon nanotubes on aluminum foil and ended up with a coating that absorbs more than 99.995 percent of light. They found it by accident, and it turned a two million dollar diamond into a flat black void.
Would you wear it? Tell us below.
thumbnail_text: A BLACK SO DARK A DIAMOND LOOKS FLAT
first_comment: Your eyes read shape from light and shadow. With almost no light coming back, the diamond loses all its shape. What would you coat in it?
